title: Cancer is a reversible shrinking of a cell's computational boundary

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cancer is a reversible shrinking of a cell's computational boundary

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cancer is a reversible shrinking of the computational boundary of the Self: by becoming isolated from surrounding tissue's physiological (bioelectric) signals, a cell's cognitive boundary shrinks to its pre-multicellular, single-cell size, so it reverts to proliferating and migrating for its own benefit.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Cancer is a (reversible) shrinking of the computational boundary of a biosystem: by isolating itself from the surrounding tissue’s physiological signals, a cell’s cognitive boundary shrinks to the small size it had before multicellularity.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Conclusion and Future Outlook”. Scope: Carcinogenic transformation in metazoan tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-21: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.51

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public cancer data can test associations and some perturbational consequences of physiological isolation. The shrinking-Self interpretation is not uniquely distinguished from standard signaling models, so only its measurable causal components are resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure long-range physiological connectivity, proliferation, and migration during transformation and reversal, testing whether restoring connectivity precedes and predicts phenotypic normalization beyond genomic and local signaling covariates.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Communication loss may be a consequence rather than a cause of cancer.

Computational boundary is not directly measurable.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.68
analysis feasibility: 0.58
data adequacy: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The conclusion identifies cancer with a reversible shrink of the Self to a unicellular cognitive scale. The laboratory patterns cited for it, depolarization-linked overgrowth and hyperpolarization-linked suppression, are equally described as membrane-potential effects on cell behavior. No existing observation counts for one description and against the other. The cognitive identification is not empirically resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Isolation from bioelectric signals, proliferation, and migration are measurable, and so is reversal when coupling is restored. Those outcomes are also predicted by voltage-dependent control of growth without any shrinking cognitive boundary.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Reversibility of a phenotype does not measure the size of a Self.

The computational-boundary wording does not change the predicted tumor phenotypes.

fields.label: Dimension scores

data existence: 0.08
data adequacy: 0.08
discriminating power: 0.15
operationalizability: 0.3
